extracted.intended_audience: advanced students/researchers of classical mechanics and fluid dynamics (readers of Newtonian-style treatises)
extracted.subtask_description: Analytical propositions and geometric constructions describing projectile and orbital motion in media with resistance (linear and quadratic), density laws, and basic hydrostatics; includes rules for constructing trajectories (hyperbolas, parabolas, spirals) from given physical conditions. Targeted at deriving forces, densities, velocities, and geometric loci.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reg. 1
rubrics_metrics.description: Si servetur Medii densitas in A & mutetur angulus NAH, manebunt longitudines AH, AI, HX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If medium density at A is held fixed and the launch angle NAH is varied, the lengths AH, AI, HX remain invariant; thus if those lengths are found in one case, the hyperbola for any other NAH can be determined directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reg. 2
rubrics_metrics.description: Si servetur tum angulus NAH tum Medii densitas in A, & mutetur velocitas quacum corpus projicitur; servabitur longitudo AH, & mutabitur AI in duplicata ratione velocitatis reciproce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: With both angle and medium density fixed, changing the projectile speed leaves AH fixed while AI changes inversely with the square of the speed (AI ∝ 1/v^2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reg. 3
rubrics_metrics.description: Si tam angulus NAH quam corporis velocitas in A, gravitasq; acceleratrix servetur, & proportio resistentiæ in A ad gravitatem motricem augeatur in ratione, quacunque: augebitur proportio AH ad AI eadem ratione, manente Parabolæ latere recto, eiq; proportionali longitudine AHq. ÷ AI; & propterea minuetur AH in eadem ratione, & AI minuetur in ratione illa duplicata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When angle, launch speed, and accelerating gravity are fixed but the ratio of resistance to gravity at A changes, AH:AI changes in the same ratio; AH decreases proportionally and AI decreases in the squared sense. Also notes interplay between medium density, specific gravity, and resistance magnitude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reg. 4
rubrics_metrics.description: Quoniam densitas Medii prope verticem Hyperbolæ major est quam in loco A, ut servetur densitas mediocris, debet ratio minimæ tangentium GT ad Tangentem AH inveniri, & densitas in A, per Regulam tertiam, diminui in ratione paulo minore quam semisummæ Tangentium ad Tangentium AH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To preserve an average density when density near the hyperbola vertex is larger than at A, the minimal tangent GT to AH must be found; density at A should be reduced slightly less than the semi-sum ratio of tangents. This gives a practical correction procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reg. 5
rubrics_metrics.description: Si dantur longitudines AH, AI, & describenda sit figura AGK: produc HN ad X, ut sit HX æqualis facto sub n + 1 & AI; centroq; X & Asymptotis MX, NX per punctum A describatur Hyperbola, ea lege ut sit AI ad quamvis VG ut XV^n ad XI^n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction rule: given AH and AI, construct HX = (n+1)·AI, set center X and asymptotes MX, NX, then describe the hyperbola through A so that AI : VG = XV^n : XI^n. Provides a geometric construction tailored to the chosen exponent n.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reg. 6
rubrics_metrics.description: Quo major est numerus n, eo magis accuratæ sunt hæ Hyperbolæ in ascensu corporis ab A, & minus accuratæ in ejus descensu ad G; & contra. Hyperbola Conica mediocrem rationem tenet, estq; cæteris simplicior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on choice of exponent n: larger n gives hyperbolas that better approximate ascending motion from A but worse approximation for descent toward G. The conic hyperbola (n appropriate) is a moderate and simpler compromise. Gives practical advice for modeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reg. 7
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodus expedita determinandi hanc Hyperbolam ex Phænomenis: projiciantur corpora duo similia & æqualia eadem velocitate in angulis diversis ... notetur proportio AK ad Ak = d : e; perpendiculo AI erecto ... collige graphice longitudines AK, Ak ... si ratio AK:Ak = d:e then AH choice is correct; otherwise take further steps (SM, MN construction) to find AH by intersections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An experimental/graphical procedure: fire two identical projectiles at different angles, measure impact distances AK, Ak, compare to expected ratio d:e; use perpendiculars and auxiliary constructions to iteratively find AH that makes observed ratios match predictions. Practical measurement and correction method for deducing the hyperbola from experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reg. 8
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventis longitudinibus AH, HX; si jam desideretur positio rectæ AH, secundum quam Projectile data illa cum velocitate emissum incidit in punctum quodvis K: ad puncta A & K erigantur rectæ AC, KF horizonti perpendiculares, quarum AC deorsum tendat, & æquetur ipsi AI seu ½HX. Asymptotis AK, KF describatur Hyperbola, cujus Conjugata transeat per punctum C, centroq; A & intervallo AH describatur Circulus secans Hyperbolam illam in puncto H; & projectile secundum rectam AH emissum incidet in punctum K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometric construction to locate the launch line AH for which a projectile fired from A with given speed lands at K: erect perpendiculars, set AC = AI = 1/2 HX, draw hyperbola with asymptotes AK and KF such that its conjugate passes through C, then the circle centered at A radius AH intersects hyperbola at H. This yields the required AH.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholium on Hyperbolae vs Parabolas
rubrics_metrics.description: Quoniam motus non fit in Parabola nisi in Medio non resistente, in Hyperbolis vero hic descriptis fit per resistentiam perpetuam; perspicuum est quod linea, quam Projectile in Medio uniformiter resistente describit, propius accedit ad Hyperbolas hasce quam ad Parabolam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretive guidance: in uniformly resisting media, projectile paths are hyperbolic rather than parabolic; the trajectories found are hyperbolic-type but differ near the vertex and asymptotes. Practical note: hyperbolas derived here can be used approximately in mechanics; rules give how to adapt constructions for parabolas when density law is reciprocal to tangent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitio Fluidi
rubrics_metrics.description: Fluidum est corpus omne cujus partes cedunt vi cuicunque illatæ, & cedendo facile movetur inter se.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition: a fluid is any body whose parts yield to any impressed force and move easily among themselves. This foundational definition underlies subsequent hydrostatic propositions and arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XI (Theor. VIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Si corpus resistitur partim in ratione velocitatis, partim in velocitatis ratione duplicata, & sola vi insita in Medio similari movetur, sumantur autem tempora in progressione Arithmetica: quantitates velocitatibus reciproce proportionales, data quadam quantitate auctæ, erunt in progressione Geometrica.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mathematical principle: when resistance is a sum of linear and quadratic terms in velocity and intrinsic medium force acts, if equal time increments form an arithmetic progression, then quantities reciprocally proportional to velocities (with an added constant) form a geometric progression. The proposition provides a way to represent velocity variation via hyperbolic areas and series expansions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XII (Theor. IX)
rubrics_metrics.description: Iisdem positis, dico quod si spatia descripta sumantur in progressione Arithmetica, velocitates data quadam quantitate auctæ erunt in progressione Geometrica.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If distances traversed grow arithmetically under the same hypotheses, then the velocities (with a given additive quantity) will form a geometric progression. Corollaries explain how to obtain velocity from a given time-area hyperbolic representation and vice versa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XIII (Theor. X)
rubrics_metrics.description: Posito quod corpus ab uniformi gravitate deorsum attractum recta ascendit vel descendit, & resistitur partim in ratione velocitatis, partim in ejusdem ratione duplicata: dico quod si Circuli & Hyperbolæ diametris parallelæ rectæ per conjugatarum diametrorum terminos ducantur, & velocitates sint ut segmenta quædam parallelarum a dato puncto ducta, Tempora erunt ut arearum Sectores, rectis a centro ad segmentorum terminos ductis abscissi: & contra.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes geometric correspondences between velocities, areas (circular sectors or hyperbolic sectors), and times for ascent/descent under gravity with combined linear and quadratic resistance. Three cases (using circles or hyperbolas depending on signs of gravitational term) provide constructions for time as area and relate velocity decrements to resistance expressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XIV (Prob. IV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Iisdem positis, dico quod spatium ascensu vel descensu descriptum, est ut summa vel differentia areæ per quam tempus exponitur, & areæ cujusdam alterius quæ augetur vel diminuitur in progressione Arithmetica; si vires ex resistentia & gravitate compositæ sumantur in progressione Geometrica.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives formula relating the space ascended/descended to the sum/difference of an area representing time and another area that increases/decreases arithmetically, under the condition that the combined forces (resistance and gravity) form a geometric progression. Includes corollary comparing displacements in resisting vs non-resisting media.

rubrics_metrics.name: LEM. III (Spiral lemma)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sit PQRr Spiralis quæ secet radios omnes SP, SQ, SR, &c. in æqualibus angulis. ... ultima ratio rectanguli TQ × PS ad PQ quad. erit ratio æqualitatis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometric lemma about a spiral cutting radii under equal angles: derives relation TQ × PS = PQ^2 (i.e., PQ^2 equals rectangle TQ × PS) by considering limiting coalescence of points. Used to relate tangents and chord elements in spiral motions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XV (Theor. XI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Si Medii densitas in locis singulis sit reciproce ut distantia locorum a centro immobili, sitque vis centripeta in duplicata ratione densitatis: dico quod corpus gyrari potest in Spirali, quæ radios omnes a centro illo ductos intersecat in angulo dato.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows that if medium density ∝ 1/(distance) and centripetal force ∝ (density)^2, a body can move in a spiral cutting radii at a given angle. Corollaries give: velocity at P equals that for a circular orbit at same radius; density expressions in terms of OS, OP; ratio of resisting to centripetal force equals 1/2 OS:OP; conditions for gyration (resistance must be < half centripetal) and consequences for descent times and revolution counts. Provides methods to infer density or centripetal force from observed spiral motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XVI (Theor. XII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Si Medii densitas in locis singulis sit reciproce ut dignitas aliqua distantiæ locorum a centro, sitque vis centripeta reciproce ut distantia in dignitatem illam ducta: dico quod corpus gyrari potest in Spirali, quæ radios omnes a centro illo ductos intersecat in angulo dato.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generalizes Prop. XV to densities ∝ 1/SP^n and centripetal ∝ 1/SP^{n+1} (index n+1). Demonstrates that time to describe arc PQ scales as PQ × SP^{n/2} and derives the corresponding density law. Useful for tailoring spiral orbits to arbitrary power-law density and centripetal force laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XVII (Prob. V)
rubrics_metrics.description: Invenire & vim centripetam & Medii resistentiam qua corpus in data Spirali data lege revolvi potest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Problem: given a spiral and the velocity along it, determine the centripetal force and medium resistance/density required. Method: use infinitesimal arc velocity, centripetal altitude TQ ∝ centripetal×time^2, and area differences for retardation to extract resistance and density.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XVIII (Prob. VI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Data lege vis centripetæ, invenire Medii densitatem in locis singulis, qua corpus datam Spiralem describet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inverse problem: given the centripetal force law, find the medium density function that causes a body to follow a prescribed spiral. Procedure: compute local velocities from centripetal law, then deduce density from observed velocity retardation as in Prop. XVII.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XIX (Theor. XIII) — Hydrostatic equality
rubrics_metrics.description: Fluidi homogenei & immoti, quod in vase quocunque immoto clauditur & undique comprimitur, partes omnes (seposita Condensationis, gravitatis & virium omnium centripetarum consideratione) æqualiter premuntur undique, & absque omni motu a pressione illa orto permanent in locis suis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hydrostatic principle: in a homogeneous, static fluid enclosed in any rigid vessel and subjected to uniform compression, every part is equally pressed in all directions and remains at rest. The proposition is demonstrated by contradiction through spherical partitioning and further corollaries: pressure equality across parts, inability of pressure to create internal motion absent compression changes, and implications for transmission of pressure to vessel walls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XX (Theor. XIV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Si Fluidi Sphærici, & in æqualibus a centro distantiis homogenei, fundo sphærico concentrico incumbentis partes singulæ versus centrum totius gravitent; sustinet fundum pondus Cylindri, cujus basis æqualis est superficiei fundi, & altitudo eadem quæ Fluidi incumbentis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hydrostatic load result: the spherical bottom sustains only the weight of a cylinder whose base equals the area of the bottom and whose height equals the depth of fluid above—i.e., pressure on the bottom equals that of a column of fluid of same base and height. Corollaries: bottom is not loaded by the entire fluid weight (some supported by arching/side pressures), pressure on equal-distance spherical surfaces is equal regardless of orientation or internal channels, and conclusions extend to varying gravity or nonuniform fluid density by similar reasoning.
